items.title: Live: Iran opens fire on ships travelling through Strait of Hormuz
items.description: The two Indian-flagged vessels reported being fired upon by gunboats from Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps, just a day after the strait was declared open by Iran's foreign minister. Follow live.

items.title: Donald Trump might have annoyed the only ally who can help clear sea mines
items.description: The prospect of mines in the Strait of Hormuz has highlighted a gap in US naval capabilities and reinforced its need for NATO help.

items.title: The mystery of an outback 'catch and kill' squad during WWII has been solved
items.description: In the 1940s, a shadowy military unit was assembled to catch and kill Japanese soldiers on Australia's remote northern coast. The identity of the so-called Solomons Six was a mystery — until now.

items.title: The quiet disappearance of Australia's rainfall observation network
items.description: For more than 60 years, Frank Pritchard has diligently checked the weather, adding to a record that stretches back more than a century. But he's part of a quietly shrinking network of observers around Australia. Without it, scientists say we risk missing out on important information that could help improve weather forecast models and climate projections.

items.title: Crackdown on unregistered NDIS providers coming in bid to save $6b a year
items.description: NDIS Minister Mark Butler will announce reforms to the disability scheme on Wednesday that will aim to save more than $6 billion a year by 2035 — and the largely unregulated market of NDIS providers is at the top of his reform list.

items.title: How Trump turned on the first US-born Pope
items.description: US President Donald Trump described Pope Leo XIV's accession to the papacy as a meaningful moment for America. But now he has said the pontiff is hurting the Catholic Church, and is weak. Here's how their relationship has developed over the lpst year.

items.title: Out at sea, 35 million barrels of oil buffer Japan from the fuel crisis
items.description: Japan has oil stockpile sites littered around the country, and as the world faces a fuel crisis, neighbours in Asia have been turning to Tokyo for assistance.

items.title: Who's really behind 'Big Australia'? Taylor's high immigration stance raises eyebrows
items.description: Angus Taylor's criticism of high immigration puts a strange spotlight on his own party's policy legacy.

items.title: The myths of motherhood and the damage they do
items.description: I traced my family's maternal line from a home for abandoned children in Italy to my own wheelchair, confronting the myths we cling to about what makes a good mother — and the damage they do.

items.title: Egypt, Pakistan building framework for lasting US-Iran peace

featured_image.name: Saudi, Pakistani, Egyptian FMs to join Türkiye talks at ...

items.description:
Egypt's Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty confirmed on Saturday that Egypt and Pakistan are working closely together on a framework to secure a lasting peace between the United States and Iran, as four regional powers intensify diplomacy ahead of a ceasefire deadline set to expire on April 22.[1]

Abdelatty said Egypt, Turkey, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia are coordinating on a broader regional initiative aimed at preventing further escalation and building a post-conflict security arrangement. He stressed the need to protect Gulf nations and ensure the stability of energy markets, supply chains, and food security.[1]

items.title: Iranians face 50th day of internet blackout as ceasefire nears expiration

featured_image.name: Ceasefire brings some relief for Iranians but economic outlook ...

items.description: As a two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran inches toward its April 22 expiration, Iranians are navigating a precarious existence shaped by weeks of aerial bombardment, a brutal government crackdown on mass protests, and an economic crisis with no clear end in sight. The pause in fighting has brought a measure of relief — but for many, it has also sharpened fears that the worst may still lie ahead.

items.title: Iranians fear regime will tighten grip once ceasefire holds

featured_image.name: Military Parade Of Iran's SelfSacrificing Daughters

items.description:
Iranians struggling to piece together daily life after weeks of U.S. and Israeli airstrikes and a brutal crackdown on protesters are gripped by fear that conditions will only worsen once the guns fall silent, even as a fragile ceasefire offers a momentary reprieve.

"The war will end, but that's when our real problems with the system begin," a 37-year-old named Fariba who took part in the January unrest told Reuters by phone from Iran. "I'm very afraid that if the regime reaches an agreement with the United States, it will increase pressure on ordinary people."[1]

items.title: Iran's 'mosquito fleet' holds Hormuz despite 155 warships sunk

featured_image.name: Why Iran has a speedboat swarm that's punching above its ...

items.description: Nearly two months after the United States and Israel launched Operation Epic Fury against Iran on February 28, U.S. and allied strikes have sunk more than 155 Iranian naval vessels and wiped out entire classes of warships. Yet the fleet Tehran relies on most to control the Strait of Hormuz — a sprawling armada of small, fast boats operated by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps — remains largely intact and continues to menace one of the world's most critical shipping lanes.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Japan, Australia sign deal for production of first three frigates
items.description: Defence Minister Richard Marles and his Japanese counterpart, Koizumi Shinjirō, signed the deal aboard one of the warships docked in Melbourne.

items.title: Australia, Japan sign $7B stealth frigate deal

featured_image.name: Australia to seek deal with Japan in frigate development talks

items.description: Australia and Japan on Saturday signed contracts launching a A$10 billion (US$7 billion) deal to supply Australia with advanced stealth frigates, in what has been described as Japan's most consequential defense export agreement since World War II.[1][2]

items.title: China reaches 125 GW to become world's largest nuclear power

featured_image.name: Phase 1 of world's largest nuclear power base goes live in China

items.description: China has claimed the top spot globally for total installed nuclear power capacity, reaching 125 gigawatts, according to a blue book released Friday by the China Nuclear Energy Association. The milestone underscores Beijing's accelerating push to expand its atomic energy fleet at a pace unmatched by any other nation.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump reverses course, renews Russian oil sanctions waiver

featured_image.name: Trump ups sanctions on Russian oil

items.description:
The Trump administration on Friday issued a new month-long waiver allowing countries to purchase sanctioned Russian oil and petroleum products at sea, reversing its stated position just two days after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Washington had no plans to do so.[1][2]

The U.S. Treasury Department posted the license to its website late on April 17, permitting countries to buy Russian oil loaded on vessels as of that date through May 16. The license excludes transactions involving Iran, Cuba, and North Korea.[2]

items.title: Israeli fire kills two UNICEF water truck drivers in Gaza

featured_image.name: UNICEF says Israeli fire kills two Gaza water truck drivers ...

items.description: UNICEF said Friday it was "outraged" after two truck drivers it contracted to deliver clean water to families in the Gaza Strip were killed by Israeli fire at the Mansoura water filling point in northern Gaza. Two others were injured in the incident, which occurred during routine water trucking operations early Friday morning, according to the agency's statement.[1][2][3]

items.title: Israeli drone kills one in southern Lebanon hours into ceasefire

featured_image.name: Israeli drone attack kills 1 in southern Lebanon despite ceasefire deal

items.description:
An Israeli drone struck a motorcycle in southern Lebanon on Friday, killing one person on the first full day of a US-brokered 10-day ceasefire, even as President Trump declared on social media that Israel was "PROHIBITED" from bombing Lebanon.

Lebanon's state-run National News Agency reported that a motorcyclist was killed in the town of Kounine, in the Bint Jbeil district, after being targeted by an Israeli drone. The Lebanese army reported additional violations on Friday morning, including intermittent shelling of several southern villages and firing on an ambulance team in Kounine.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: Iran threatens to reclose Strait of Hormuz if US blockade continues

featured_image.name: Ships crossing Hormuz need OK from IRGC, unfreezing funds ...

items.description: Hours after declaring the Strait of Hormuz fully reopened to commercial shipping, Iran warned on Friday that it could shut the waterway again if the United States maintains its naval blockade of Iranian ports, escalating a standoff over one of the world's most vital energy corridors.

items.description: President Trump states the U.S. military conducted its first known airstrike inside Venezuela targeting a dock where drugs were allegedly loaded onto boats[1][2][4].

items.description: President Trump met with Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu to discuss advancing phase two of the Gaza ceasefire, including reconstruction and responses to Iran[1][4].

items.description: Federal agencies including DHS, FBI, and ICE investigate $110 million in suspected fraud at Minnesota child care centers following a viral YouTube video[3].

items.description: Public backlash against AI infrastructure data centers grows, with protests and demands for bans influencing Democratic Party strategies for future elections[3].

items.description: China prioritizes humanoid robots in tech race with U.S., ramping up production while warning of industry bubble and potential bottlenecks[3].

items.description: President Trump spoke with Putin amid ongoing Ukraine conflict, with Russia reevaluating peace plan tenets after Ukrainian denials[1].
